_what_this_is: The SDK floor and the test-runner mode. Neither entry is a pin. The version below is a FLOOR with rollForward=latestMajor, which takes the newest installed SDK and fails loudly on a machine that is behind -- the opposite of a ceiling. See STACK.md, 'The build configuration'.
_the_test_entry_is_not_a_version: TUnit is MTP-only. The MTP mode of 'dotnet test' is opted into here and nowhere else (.NET 10 SDK and later; Microsoft Learn, looked up 2026-08-16). Without it 'dotnet test' runs the VSTest path and errors out against an MTP v2 test project.
_provenance: Floor recorded 2026-08-16 against the SDK then installed on this machine. Raising it is a decision; a machine with a newer SDK needs no change here, because rollForward already takes it. Corrected 2026-09-14 (previously "against the SDK installed on this machine (10.0.302, dotnet --list-sdks)") -- that clause named the floor and the installed SDK as one number, and they have not been the same number since this machine moved on. Re-read 2026-09-14: `dotnet --list-sdks` reports 10.0.401 and nothing else, `dotnet --version` agrees, and the newest Microsoft.NETCore.App is 10.0.12. rollForward=latestMajor took it with no edit here, which is the property this entry exists to record -- and taking it is what re-resolved the Microsoft.Extensions / ILCompiler / ILLink family from 10.0.11 to 10.0.12. THE FLOOR BELOW IS DELIBERATELY UNMOVED: it is the version a machine must have at least, not the version this one happens to run, and raising it would refuse machines nothing has found a reason to refuse.
